extracted.intended_audience: publishers and literary agents submitting books to the PEN America Literary Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility criteria for publishers/agents to submit books and translations to the PEN America Literary Awards, including technical submission requirements, fees, and award-specific evaluative emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date window
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted books must be published by a trade or academic publisher between January 1 and December 31 in the applicable year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books published outside that calendar window are ineligible for that year's cycle. Galleys or advance copies are accepted if the book will be published after the deadline (see FAQs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible publisher types
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must be published by a trade or academic publisher; self-published books are ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly states 'Self-published books are ineligible for the PEN America Literary Awards.' It also notes that 'trade publisher' includes academic presses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission source (who may submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: PEN America will only accept submissions from publishers or literary agents; authors may not submit their own books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit via the submission form and select the award you are submitting to. Publishers and agents may submit multiple titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-author works ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Books with more than one original author are ineligible for the PEN America Literary Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award selection on form & multiple-award restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: On the submission form, submitters must select the award they are submitting to; books cannot be submitted to multiple awards in the same cycle except for the PEN Open Book Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting to the PEN Open Book Award, complete a separate submission. Translated books are not eligible for the PEN Open Book Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide verified email addresses on the submission form and additional contacts so PEN America can contact authors/translators if longlisted, a finalist, or a winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders cannot be processed without an email address. Add [email protected] to your address book as the main point of contact from PEN America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript file format and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a PDF file of the galley or final manuscript; book award submissions will be read as PDF files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save the file as BOOKTITLE_AUTHORNAME. For the judges’ convenience, upload a book file WITHOUT watermarks. Each book file will be kept confidentially between the Literary Awards team and the awards judges. PEN America may request a physical copy if a book is longlisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book jacket image requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a high-resolution book jacket photo with the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the book cover is not yet finalized, upload a note indicating such and email the cover when available to [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission fee and payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission is $85 and submission fees are not refundable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All payments must be made via the submission form. Do not submit your title before requesting a fee exemption (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee waiver eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission fees may be waived for publishers whose annual net sales are less than $2 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request an exemption via the provided form which asks for a letter on company letterhead stating the press’s annual net sales are less than $2 million. PEN America will provide an alternative submission method if you request exemption before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for judging and announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges read through the fall; longlists and finalists are announced in winter; winners are announced in the spring at the Literary Awards Ceremony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judges' reading and deliberation process spans months; plan submission timing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance/galleys accepted when book not yet published
rubrics_metrics.description: If a book will not be published until after the deadline, galleys and advance copies are accepted in place of the finished book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FAQs for instructions on submitting galleys or advance copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility varies by award (residency/citizenship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Residency and citizenship requirements vary depending on each award; consult the 'Who is Eligible' section of each award's page for specifics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some awards have geographic or citizenship limitations; the PEN/E.O. Wilson award is noted as the only book award open to publishers outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. publisher definition (office location)
rubrics_metrics.description: A press is considered a U.S. publisher only if it has offices located within the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a press is based outside the U.S. but distributes in the U.S., it is not considered a U.S. publisher for eligibility purposes (with named exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest and PEN affiliation ineligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Current PEN America staff, interns, donors, committee co-chairs, judges, and Trustees are not eligible for Awards and/or Grants; current members of the Literary Awards Committee are also ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past involvement does not result in disqualification; the writer must not have been connected with PEN America in the specified roles during the calendar years of the applicable awards cycle (example given).

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN America membership status does not confer advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: PEN America Members are eligible for Awards and Grants but will not be given preferential consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations sources and judge nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are provided by Members and/or by anonymous nomination panels; judges are encouraged to nominate their own honorees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All eligible books and nominations are considered; panels reach decisions after months of reading, email conversation, and conference calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and judge qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards call on over 80 judges (writers, editors, critics) who read submitted books and deliberate; decisions are made after extended reading and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers are asked to send their very best books. The program estimates over 1,300 books received each year and emphasizes diligent reading and conversation among judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Jean Stein Book Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes a book-length work of any genre for its originality, merit, and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award is annual and evaluates a book's originality, literary merit, and broader impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Robert W. Bingham Prize (debut short story collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors an exceptionally talented fiction writer whose debut book represents distinguished literary achievement and suggests significant promise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted at debut short story collections; emphasizes distinguished literary achievement and future promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Robert J. Dau Short Story Prize criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes emerging fiction writers each year for their debut short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twelve emerging fiction writers are recognized annually; focuses on debut short story quality and emerging talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Voelcker Award for Poetry criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Given to a poet whose distinguished and growing body of work to date represents a notable and accomplished presence in American literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates a poet’s cumulative body of work (distinguished and growing), not a single book necessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Mike Nichols Writing for Performance Award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Confers a prize to a writer whose work exemplifies excellence and influence in the world of performance writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award emphasizes both excellence and demonstrable influence in performance writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Laura Pels International Foundation for Theater Award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards an American playwright in mid-career with an outstanding voice working indisputably at the highest level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets mid-career playwrights with an outstanding voice and demonstrated high-level achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/E.O. Wilson Literary Science Writing Award criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates writing that exemplifies literary excellence on the subject of the physical or biological sciences and communicates complex ideas clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates both literary quality and the ability to communicate complex scientific subjects to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Diamonstein-Spielvogel Award for the Art of the Essay criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors a seasoned writer whose collection of essays is an expansion or demonstration of the art of the essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focused on collections of essays and depth of essayistic craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Jacqueline Bograd Weld Award for Biography criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for excellence in the art of biography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates biographical craft and achievement; prize amount cited on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/John Kenneth Galbraith Award for Nonfiction criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded to the author of a distinguished book of nonfiction possessing notable literary merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual prize that emphasizes literary merit in nonfiction works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation awards: PEN Award for Poetry in Translation and PEN Translation Prize criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize book-length translations of poetry or translations from any language into English; PEN Translation Prize requires publication during the current calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PEN Award for Poetry in Translation recognizes book-length poetry translations; PEN Translation Prize accepts book-length translations published during the current calendar year; upload and publication eligibility rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEN/Ralph Manheim Award for Translation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Given every three years to a translator whose career has demonstrated a commitment to excellence through the body of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates a translator’s career-long commitment to excellence rather than a single work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of winner seal for publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers of winning titles that wish to use a winner seal on printed books or a digital file of the seal should contact PEN America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact [email protected] for permissions and assets related to winner seals for future print runs.
